scope_note: This is a CURATED KNOWLEDGE BASE, not an emission-factor dataset. Nothing in this file is sourced from CEA v22.0, EPA 2025 or UK 2026, and no value here is ever presented as if it were. Carbon impact is never stored as a tonnage: it is stored as a MECHANISM that the deterministic engine applies to the factory's own verified footprint. Where a mechanism cannot be defended, impact_model is NOT_QUANTIFIED and the product says so.
verification_policy: Every record carries evidence with source_name, source_title, source_url, publication_year and confidence. Records whose evidence has verification_required = true were curated from domain knowledge and MUST have their citation checked against the primary document before the number is used in an external report. The UI shows these as 'Source needs verification'.

interventions.name: Rooftop solar PV
interventions.summary: Install a grid-tied rooftop solar array to displace grid electricity drawn during daylight production hours.
technical_constraints: Requires unshaded roof or ground area of roughly 8-10 m2 per kWp installed
Roof structure must take the additional dead and wind load - a structural assessment is mandatory
Net-metering or captive-consumption approval from the state DISCOM is required and the rules differ by state
Output is daytime-only; it displaces nothing on a night shift unless storage is added
Self-consumption ratio falls sharply if array size exceeds the daytime base load
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Substitutes a depletable, high-carbon energy input with a renewable flow, reducing the embodied carbon of every downstream process without changing the process itself.
interventions.impact_basis: Generation is CALCULATED, not assumed: kWp installed x specific yield (kWh/kWp/year) for the site's latitude band, capped at the share of annual consumption that can be self-consumed in daylight hours. The displaced kWh are then valued at the factory's own resolved CEA grid factor, so the carbon result comes from verified data. Specific-yield range 1300-1600 kWh/kWp/year covers most of India; confirm with a site-specific yield assessment.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: installed cost per kWp for grid-tied commercial rooftop systems in India, inclusive of structure and net-metering work. Must be replaced with at least two local EPC quotations before any investment decision. Savings are valued at the factory's own stated electricity tariff, not at an assumed tariff.
prerequisites: Twelve months of electricity bills for load profiling

evidence.claim: Photovoltaic output at a site is the product of installed capacity and location-specific specific yield; self-consumption is limited by the coincidence of generation with load.
evidence.source_title: IEC 61724-1: Photovoltaic system performance - Monitoring

evidence.claim: Rooftop solar is an established commercial technology for Indian industrial consumers, supported by national programme frameworks and state net-metering regulation.
evidence.source_name: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, Government of India
evidence.source_title: Grid Connected Rooftop Solar Programme

interventions.name: LED lighting retrofit
interventions.summary: Replace metal-halide, sodium-vapour and fluorescent fittings with LED luminaires and add zoning controls in low-occupancy areas.
technical_constraints: Lux levels at the working plane must still meet the applicable workplace lighting standard after the retrofit
Colour rendering matters for visual inspection stations - do not specify low-CRI fittings there
High-bay fittings over hot processes need a luminaire rated for the ambient temperature
The saving is only as large as the lighting share of the site's electricity, which must be measured, not assumed
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Cuts energy demand at source and extends replacement intervals, reducing both the operational carbon and the throughput of luminaires through the waste stream.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction = lighting share of site electricity x saving on that sub-load. EcoForge defaults the lighting share to 10 % and FLAGS IT AS AN ASSUMPTION THAT MUST BE CONFIRMED from a load survey or a lighting inventory; the 45-65 % saving band on the replaced load reflects the efficacy gap between discharge lamps and current LED luminaires. The resulting kWh are valued at the factory's own resolved grid factor.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Cost depends entirely on fitting count, mounting height and wiring condition. EcoForge requires a luminaire schedule (count, wattage, type, mounting height) before it will price this.
prerequisites: Luminaire inventory or lighting load survey

evidence.claim: LED luminaires deliver substantially higher luminous efficacy than discharge and fluorescent sources, and lighting retrofits are a standard first-tier industrial energy efficiency measure.
evidence.source_title: Energy Efficiency 2023

interventions.name: Variable frequency drives on fans, blowers and pumps
interventions.summary: Fit VFDs to centrifugal fans, blowers and pumps that currently run at fixed speed with throttling or damper control, so flow is matched to demand.
interventions.current_material: Fixed-speed motor with damper or throttle control
interventions.alternative: Variable frequency drive with demand-linked control
technical_constraints: Only applies to variable-flow centrifugal loads. Positive-displacement and constant-torque loads see little or no benefit
The motor must be inverter-duty rated or be re-insulated, otherwise winding failure risk rises
Harmonic distortion must be assessed against the supply; filters or line reactors may be needed
No benefit where the fan or pump genuinely runs at full duty for the whole shift
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Eliminates energy that is currently generated and then destroyed across a damper or throttle valve, removing waste at the point where it is created rather than treating it downstream.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction = variable-flow motor share of site electricity x saving on that sub-load. The physical basis is the fan law: shaft power varies roughly with the cube of speed, so modest speed reduction on a throttled load yields a large power reduction. EcoForge defaults the variable-flow motor share to 25 % and FLAGS IT FOR CONFIRMATION from the motor list; the 15-30 % band is deliberately conservative against the theoretical cube law because real duty cycles are rarely ideal.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: drive, enclosure, cabling and commissioning per kW of motor rating. Requires the motor schedule (rating, duty, control method) and at least one local quotation before use in a decision.
prerequisites: Motor schedule with ratings, duty cycle and current control method

evidence.claim: Variable speed drives on centrifugal fan and pump loads reduce energy use because shaft power scales approximately with the cube of rotational speed; motor-driven systems are the largest single electricity end-use in industry.
evidence.source_title: Energy-Efficiency Policy Opportunities for Electric Motor-Driven Systems

evidence.claim: Motor efficiency classes and inverter-duty requirements are defined in international standards, which govern whether an existing motor can accept a drive.
evidence.source_title: IEC 60034-30-1: Efficiency classes of line operated AC motors (IE code)

interventions.name: Compressed air leak survey and pressure optimisation
interventions.summary: Ultrasonic leak survey, tagged repair programme, and reduction of system set pressure to the minimum the plant actually needs.
interventions.current_material: Leaking distribution network at elevated set pressure
interventions.alternative: Sealed network at optimised set pressure with zone isolation
technical_constraints: Pressure can only be lowered to the highest minimum requirement on the network - one high-pressure user forces the whole system up unless it is isolated or boosted locally
Leak repair is a recurring programme, not a one-off project; savings decay without it
Requires a flow meter or at least loaded-hours logging to verify the saving afterwards
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Removes pure waste: energy consumed to compress air that never does useful work. Nothing is substituted and nothing new is built.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction = compressed-air share of site electricity x saving on that sub-load. Two mechanisms combine: eliminating leakage flow, and the roughly 6-7 % reduction in compressor power for each 1 bar of set-pressure reduction. EcoForge defaults the compressed-air share to 15 % and FLAGS IT FOR CONFIRMATION from compressor nameplate data and loaded hours.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: cost of an ultrasonic survey plus a repair campaign for a single-site SME network. Highly dependent on network length and how many leaks are found. Obtain a survey quotation.
prerequisites: Compressor nameplate data and loaded-hours log

evidence.claim: Leakage and excessive set pressure are the dominant sources of avoidable energy loss in industrial compressed air systems, and systematic leak detection with pressure optimisation is the standard remedy.
evidence.source_name: US Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office
evidence.source_title: Improving Compressed Air System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry

evidence.claim: Energy assessment methodology for compressed air systems is standardised, which is what makes a claimed saving verifiable after implementation.
evidence.source_title: ISO 11011: Compressed air - Energy efficiency - Assessment

interventions.name: Flue gas waste heat recovery
interventions.summary: Recover sensible heat from furnace or heat-treatment flue gas to pre-heat combustion air, charge material or process water.
interventions.alternative: Recuperator or economiser recovering sensible heat
technical_constraints: Requires a sustained flue temperature high enough to be worth recovering and a co-located heat sink that needs the heat at the same time
Acid dew-point corrosion limits how far flue gas can be cooled when the fuel contains sulphur
Dust loading in foundry flue gas fouls heat exchanger surfaces and forces a cleaning regime
Space and duct routing around an existing furnace is frequently the binding constraint
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Closes an energy loop inside the plant: an output stream that is currently discarded becomes an input to the same or an adjacent process.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction applies to the fuel fired in the furnace served by the recovery unit. The 8-20 % band reflects combustion-air pre-heating on a typical fuel-fired furnace; the actual figure is set by flue temperature, flow and the load profile of the heat sink, so a flue gas survey (temperature, flow, composition) is REQUIRED before the number is used in a decision.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Recuperator cost is dominated by duty, materials of construction and retrofit difficulty around the existing furnace. Requires an engineered quotation against a flue gas survey.
prerequisites: Flue gas survey: temperature, mass flow, dust loading, sulphur content

evidence.claim: Waste heat recovery from furnace flue gas, principally by combustion air pre-heating, is a best available technique for the foundry sector, with the achievable saving governed by flue temperature and the availability of a heat sink.
evidence.source_title: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Smitheries and Foundries Industry

interventions.name: Furnace lining and insulation upgrade
interventions.summary: Replace degraded refractory with low thermal mass ceramic fibre or microporous insulation and seal door and charging losses.
interventions.alternative: Low thermal mass ceramic fibre / microporous insulation
technical_constraints: Lining material must withstand the process temperature and be chemically compatible with the melt, slag or atmosphere
Ceramic fibre has handling and respirable-fibre controls that must be in place
Work can only be done during a planned shutdown, which sets the real schedule constraint
Low thermal mass helps batch and intermittent furnaces most; a continuously held furnace benefits less
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Reduces the energy needed per unit of product by cutting shell and opening losses, extending campaign life and reducing refractory waste per tonne melted.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction applies to the fuel fired in the relined furnace. The band reflects the range between a lining in reasonable condition and one that is visibly degraded, and is larger for batch furnaces than for continuously held ones. A thermographic survey of the furnace shell is REQUIRED to place the site inside this band.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Relining cost scales with furnace volume and lining specification. Obtain a refractory contractor quotation against the furnace drawing.

evidence.claim: Improved furnace insulation and reduced thermal mass are recognised best available techniques for reducing specific energy consumption in foundry and heat-treatment furnaces.
evidence.source_title: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Smitheries and Foundries Industry

interventions.name: Burner tuning and excess air control
interventions.summary: Trim air-to-fuel ratio against measured flue oxygen and add automatic ratio control, so the furnace stops heating surplus air.
interventions.current_material: Manually set burners with uncontrolled excess air
technical_constraints: Requires a flue gas analyser and a burner that is mechanically capable of ratio adjustment
Excess air cannot be reduced below the level needed for complete combustion - CO must be monitored, not just O2
Some processes require a specific furnace atmosphere and cannot be trimmed freely
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Removes energy spent heating air that takes no part in the process, without changing the product or the plant.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction applies to the fuel fired in the tuned furnace. The band covers the difference between a badly set burner running high excess air and one held near the stoichiometric minimum. A flue gas analysis is REQUIRED to establish where the site currently sits; a plant already running oxygen trim should expect the bottom of the band or nothing.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: analyser plus trim control retrofit on a single furnace. Varies widely with burner type and existing control system. Obtain a quotation.

evidence.claim: Controlling excess air against measured flue oxygen is a primary energy efficiency measure for fuel-fired furnaces and boilers.
evidence.source_name: US Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office
evidence.source_title: Improving Process Heating System Performance: A Sourcebook for Industry

interventions.name: Mechanical green sand reclamation
interventions.summary: Attrition-scrub and classify returned green sand so it re-enters the moulding loop instead of being landfilled and replaced with new silica sand.
technical_constraints: Mechanical reclamation removes the spent binder film only partially; loss on ignition and acid demand value must stay inside the moulding specification
Grain fineness number and grain shape drift with each cycle and must be monitored, with new sand added to hold the distribution
Not suitable on its own for chemically bonded cores, which need thermal reclamation
Dust extraction capacity must be sized for the additional attrition dust
Adds an electrical load, which partly offsets the gain in an electricity-intensive plant
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Closes the material loop inside the factory gate: the same sand grains circulate many times, so both purchased sand and landfilled waste fall together.

impact_params.material_displacement_note: Purchased new sand falls by the same proportion, but EcoForge does NOT convert that into a carbon saving because none of CEA v22.0, EPA 2025 or UK 2026 publishes an emission factor for silica sand.

interventions.impact_basis: Two separate effects, reported separately and honestly. (1) REPORTED: the tonnage of spent sand leaving the site as landfill waste falls by 55-80 %, and EcoForge recalculates the waste line with the verified treatment factor for the new route. (2) NOT QUANTIFIED: the avoided production of new silica sand is real but cannot be given a number, because there is no verified silica sand emission factor in the loaded datasets. Note also that UK 2026 waste guidance states its factors cannot be used to compare the lifecycle merit of waste management options, so the change is presented as a change in reported Scope 3 waste emissions under GHG Protocol attribution, not as a lifecycle saving.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Equipment cost scales with sand throughput per hour. The commercially meaningful saving is usually avoided new-sand purchase plus avoided disposal cost, both of which EcoForge computes from the factory's own stated prices - it does not assume them.
prerequisites: Sand testing regime: GFN, LOI, acid demand value, clay content
Current new-sand price and disposal cost

evidence.claim: Sand reclamation is a best available technique for foundries, reducing both new sand consumption and the quantity of spent sand sent for disposal; mechanical reclamation suits green sand while chemically bonded sands generally require thermal treatment.
evidence.source_title: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Smitheries and Foundries Industry

evidence.claim: Moulding sand quality for re-use is controlled by measurable properties - grain fineness number, loss on ignition, acid demand value and clay content - which is what makes reclaimed sand acceptance testable rather than assumed.
evidence.source_title: Mold and Core Test Handbook

interventions.name: Thermal sand reclamation
interventions.summary: Calcine returned sand to burn off organic binder residues, allowing reclaimed sand to be used for chemically bonded moulds and cores.
technical_constraints: Consumes fuel or electricity to reach calcination temperature, so it ADDS an energy load that must be netted off against the material benefit
Requires flue gas treatment for the combustion products of the burnt binder
Residual inorganic binder and dead clay are not removed by heat alone
Only economic above a certain sand throughput; a small jobbing foundry usually cannot justify it
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Restores spent chemically bonded sand to near-new quality, closing a loop that mechanical reclamation alone cannot close.

impact_params.added_energy_note: Calcination energy is a real cost against this intervention and is NOT netted off automatically, because the fuel and specific energy consumption depend on the equipment selected. Supply them and EcoForge will subtract the added emissions.

interventions.impact_basis: Same two-part treatment as mechanical reclamation, with a higher diversion rate. The added calcination energy is shown as an OPEN ITEM rather than silently ignored: until the equipment's fuel type and specific energy consumption are supplied, the net carbon result is incomplete and EcoForge says so.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Requires an engineered quotation including flue gas treatment.
prerequisites: Fuel type and specific energy consumption of the proposed unit

evidence.claim: Thermal reclamation removes organic binder residues and is the applicable route for chemically bonded sands, at the cost of additional energy input and flue gas treatment.
evidence.source_title: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Smitheries and Foundries Industry

interventions.name: Spent foundry sand into construction materials
interventions.summary: Route spent foundry sand to a cement, concrete block or road base producer as a partial fine-aggregate replacement instead of to landfill.
interventions.alternative: Spent foundry sand as fine aggregate in construction products
technical_constraints: The sand must pass leachate testing for the receiving application and the local regulatory consent regime
Ferrous green sand is generally more acceptable than non-ferrous or chemically bonded sand because of residual metals and binder chemistry
The receiving producer must be within economic haulage distance, and that distance carries its own transport emissions
A named, contracted offtaker is required - without one this is a pathway, not a plan

required_properties.leachate: within regulatory limits for the receiving use

interventions.circularity_mechanism: Turns a disposal liability into an input for a different industry, keeping the material in productive use and displacing virgin aggregate extraction.
interventions.impact_basis: EcoForge recalculates the waste line with the verified treatment factor for the diverted route. It does NOT claim a saving for the virgin aggregate displaced at the receiving plant, because under GHG Protocol attribution that benefit belongs to the user of the recycled material, not to the waste producer - and the UK 2026 waste guidance says so explicitly. This intervention stays POTENTIAL until a named offtaker and a consent are recorded.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: cost is testing, consent and any handling or storage change; haulage may be paid by the offtaker or by the factory depending on the commercial deal. Not a capital project in most cases.
prerequisites: Leachate characterisation of the spent sand
Named offtaker within economic haulage distance
Regulatory consent for the receiving application

evidence.claim: Spent foundry sand is used as a partial fine-aggregate substitute in construction applications where leachate characteristics are acceptable, and beneficial-use routes for foundry sand are recognised by environmental regulators.
evidence.source_title: Beneficial Uses of Spent Foundry Sands

evidence.claim: Emissions from recycling routes are attributed to the user of the recycled material rather than to the producer of the waste, so a waste producer may not claim the avoided primary production.
evidence.source_title: GHG Protocol Corporate Value Chain (Scope 3) Accounting and Reporting Standard

interventions.name: Increase verified recycled content in the metal charge
interventions.summary: Shift the furnace charge mix further towards verified recycled scrap and away from primary metal, within the constraints of the casting specification.
technical_constraints: Residual tramp elements (Cu, Sn, Cr, Ni) accumulate with scrap and are difficult to remove - the casting specification sets a hard ceiling on scrap fraction
Scrap must be segregated and of known chemistry; mixed scrap raises melt variability and rejection rates
Heavier oxide and dirt loading raises slag volume and can increase melting energy per tonne
The recycled content claim must be supported by supplier documentation, or it cannot be reported
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Substitutes a secondary material flow for a primary one, cutting upstream extraction and primary processing embodied in every tonne purchased.
interventions.impact_basis: CALCULATED from verified factors, not assumed: EcoForge re-runs the material line with a higher recycled fraction, re-resolving the UK 2026 'Material use' primary-production and closed-loop-source factors for the same material and re-weighting them by origin, exactly as the UK guidance permits. The carbon result is therefore the difference between two published factors applied to the factory's own tonnage. No avoided-burden credit is taken.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: usually a procurement and segregation change rather than a capital project; cost is scrap handling, storage segregation and incoming chemistry verification. Scrap is often cheaper than primary metal, but that price gap is market-dependent and EcoForge will not assume it - enter your own prices.
prerequisites: Casting specification limits on residual elements
Incoming scrap chemistry verification (spectrometer or supplier certificate)

evidence.claim: Material use conversion factors distinguish primary material production from closed-loop secondary source, and emissions from procured material may be apportioned by the weights of each material origin.
evidence.source_name: UK Department for Energy Security and Net Zero / Defra
evidence.source_title: UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting 2026, 'Material use' sheet guidance

evidence.claim: Accumulation of residual tramp elements is the binding technical limit on recycled content in ferrous casting, and is controlled through the casting specification.
evidence.source_title: Casting Defects Handbook / melt chemistry control guidance

interventions.name: Casting yield improvement through gating and risering redesign
interventions.summary: Simulate and redesign the gating and feeding system so that less metal is melted for each tonne of saleable casting shipped.
interventions.current_material: Metal charge at current casting yield
interventions.alternative: Metal charge at improved casting yield
technical_constraints: Feeding must still eliminate shrinkage porosity; cutting riser volume without simulation trades carbon for scrap
Requires solidification simulation capability or an experienced methoding engineer
Pattern and tooling changes are needed, which is real cost and lead time
Benefit is bounded by the casting geometry - a thick-section part has a hard yield ceiling
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Reduces the quantity of material that has to be bought, melted and re-melted per unit sold, which cuts material, energy and internal handling at the same time.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction applies to the purchased metal tonnage and, at half that proportion, to melting energy - because a share of the returns were already being re-melted internally rather than bought new. The 3-10 % band reflects typical yield headroom where no simulation has previously been done; a foundry already using simulation should expect the bottom of the band. The carbon result comes from re-running the verified material and energy factors on the reduced quantities.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: simulation study plus pattern and tooling modification for a small family of parts. Scales with the number of part numbers addressed. Obtain a quotation from a methoding consultancy.
prerequisites: Current casting yield by part number
Pattern modification budget and shutdown window

evidence.claim: Casting yield is a primary determinant of specific energy and material consumption per tonne of saleable casting, and gating and feeding optimisation supported by solidification simulation is the recognised route to improving it.
evidence.source_title: Metalcasting energy and yield improvement guidance

interventions.name: Segregated internal returns recycling
interventions.summary: Segregate runners, risers and rejected castings by alloy at source so they return directly to the furnace instead of leaving as mixed scrap.
interventions.current_material: Mixed scrap sold out, primary metal bought in
technical_constraints: Requires physical segregation discipline and labelled bins at the fettling stage - this fails without operator routine
Returns carry sand and oxide that must be removed or they raise slag volume
Alloy identity must be certain; a mis-sorted return contaminates a whole heat
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Keeps material inside the smallest possible loop - the factory itself - so it never incurs the emissions of leaving, being reprocessed elsewhere and being replaced.
interventions.impact_basis: Same calculated mechanism as recycled charge: the purchased material line is re-resolved with a higher closed-loop fraction using the published UK 2026 primary and closed-loop factors. This is a subset of the same lever, which is why it is marked as conflicting with the other two charge-mix interventions - their savings overlap and must not be added.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: bins, labelling, magnetic separation and layout change at the fettling area. Low capital, high dependence on operator routine.

evidence.claim: Segregation of internal returns by alloy at source is standard foundry practice for maintaining melt chemistry while maximising the recycled fraction of the charge.
evidence.source_title: Melt chemistry and charge make-up guidance

interventions.name: Renewable power through open access or green tariff
interventions.summary: Contract renewable electricity through state open access or a DISCOM green tariff for the share of load that solar cannot meet.
interventions.current_material: Grid electricity at the location-based grid factor
technical_constraints: Open access eligibility, banking rules, cross-subsidy surcharge and additional surcharge differ by state and change frequently
Contracted supply must be backed by tradeable instruments or a direct contract if it is to be reported at all
Requires a minimum contracted demand that many small SMEs do not meet

required_properties.instruments: renewable energy certificates or equivalent contractual instrument

interventions.circularity_mechanism: Changes the origin of the energy input without changing the process, shifting the supply chain rather than the plant.
interventions.impact_basis: DELIBERATELY NOT QUANTIFIED in this footprint. EcoForge computes a LOCATION-BASED Scope 2 figure using the CEA grid factor, and under the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance a green tariff or certificate purchase changes the MARKET-BASED figure, not the location-based one. Reporting a reduction here would be double counting against the grid average. The intervention is kept in the knowledge base because it is a legitimate and often sensible action - it simply does not move the number this product calculates, and the product says so rather than quietly crediting it.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: transaction and registration cost only; the energy cost difference depends entirely on the contracted tariff versus the current tariff and must come from real offers.
prerequisites: Contracted demand above the state open access threshold
Legal review of state open access regulations

evidence.claim: Scope 2 emissions are reported under both a location-based and a market-based method; contractual instruments such as certificates and supplier-specific contracts affect the market-based figure only.
evidence.source_title: GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance

interventions.name: Electrify gas-fired heat treatment
interventions.summary: Replace a gas-fired heat-treatment furnace with an electric resistance or induction furnace.
technical_constraints: Requires a substantial increase in sanctioned electrical load and possibly a transformer upgrade
Temperature uniformity and atmosphere control differ from a gas furnace and must be re-qualified against the heat-treatment specification
Electricity cost per useful MJ is usually higher than gas in India, so operating cost typically rises
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Shifts the process onto an energy carrier that can decarbonise over time, so the same asset gets cleaner as the grid does.

impact_params.note: The result is computed from the two factors the resolver actually returns for this factory, not assumed to be positive.

interventions.impact_basis: CALCULATED and allowed to come out NEGATIVE. EcoForge converts the gas input to useful heat at the stated furnace efficiency, converts that useful heat back to electricity input at the electric furnace efficiency, and prices it with the factory's own resolved grid factor. On the 2025-26 Indian grid factor this frequently INCREASES emissions, and EcoForge reports that rather than hiding it. The same intervention becomes attractive once the site's electricity is substantially renewable, which is exactly what the What-If Lab is for.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Furnace cost plus electrical infrastructure upgrade; requires an engineered quotation and a DISCOM load enhancement estimate.
prerequisites: Sanctioned load headroom or DISCOM enhancement

evidence.claim: Whether electrification of a thermal process reduces emissions depends on the carbon intensity of the electricity supply relative to the fuel it replaces, adjusted for the efficiency of each conversion route.
evidence.source_title: Net Zero Roadmap: industry electrification

interventions.name: Reduce diesel generator running through load management
interventions.summary: Cut DG set hours by shifting deferrable loads, improving grid-outage ride-through, and sizing standby correctly instead of running a large set on light load.
interventions.current_material: Diesel generator running on light or partial load
technical_constraints: Some loads genuinely cannot be interrupted and must stay on the DG
Running a diesel set below about 30 % load causes wet stacking and damages the engine, so light-load running is both wasteful and harmful
Depends on grid reliability, which the factory does not control
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Removes fuel burned to produce electricity that is either not needed or could have come from the grid at lower carbon intensity.
interventions.impact_basis: Reduction applies to site diesel consumption. The band reflects what load management and right-sizing typically recover where a set has been running on light load; it is bounded by how much of the running is genuinely forced by grid outages, which must be established from the DG log. Note that displaced DG electricity does not vanish - EcoForge adds it back as grid electricity at the CEA factor, so the net saving is the difference between the two routes, not the whole of the diesel.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: load management controls and metering. Right-sizing or replacing a set is a separate and much larger project.
prerequisites: DG running log with hours and load factor

evidence.claim: Diesel generating sets operated below approximately 30 % of rated load suffer incomplete combustion and cylinder glazing, with elevated specific fuel consumption.
evidence.source_title: ISO 8528: Reciprocating internal combustion engine driven alternating current generating sets

interventions.name: Fines and swarf recovery from the waste stream
interventions.summary: Recover metallic fines, swarf and grinding dust that currently leave with general waste, using magnetic separation and briquetting.
interventions.current_material: Metallic fines lost to general waste
technical_constraints: Oil-bearing swarf must be de-oiled before it can be charged, or it causes emissions and quality problems in the melt
Briquetting is needed to charge fines without unacceptable melt loss
Only worth doing above a threshold tonnage, which must be measured from a waste characterisation
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Captures a material stream that is currently lost entirely and returns it to the melt, shrinking both the waste line and the purchase line.
interventions.impact_basis: EcoForge recalculates the waste line with the verified treatment factor for the recovered route. The avoided purchase of replacement metal is handled separately through the charge-mix intervention, so the two are not added together.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: magnetic separation plus a briquetting press sized for SME throughput. Requires a waste characterisation to confirm the recoverable tonnage before quoting.
prerequisites: Waste stream characterisation with metallic fraction by mass

evidence.claim: Recovery and briquetting of metallic fines and swarf for re-melting is established practice, with de-oiling required for machining swarf before charging.
evidence.source_title: Reference Document on Best Available Techniques in the Smitheries and Foundries Industry

interventions.name: Closed-loop abrasive recovery in shot blasting
interventions.summary: Add or repair air-wash separation and classification on the shot blast machine so usable abrasive is returned to the loop instead of being discarded with the dust.
interventions.current_material: Steel shot or grit discarded with the dust fraction
technical_constraints: Operating mix (the distribution of shot sizes in circulation) determines surface finish and must be held inside specification
Dust extraction and separator settings must be balanced - over-aggressive separation throws away usable media, under-aggressive leaves fines that degrade finish
Does not apply to disposable abrasives such as garnet or slag grit used once
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Keeps the abrasive in a tight internal loop, cutting both purchase of new media and the hazardous-adjacent dust fraction leaving the site.
interventions.impact_basis: Carbon impact requires facility-specific assessment. None of CEA v22.0, EPA 2025 or UK 2026 publishes an emission factor for steel shot or abrasive media, so EcoForge cannot put a verified number on the avoided purchase. The intervention is still surfaced because the technical case and the cost case are strong and independent of the carbon number.
interventions.cost_basis: Verified data unavailable. Typically a separator repair or upgrade on an existing machine; obtain a quotation from the machine supplier.

evidence.claim: Efficient air-wash separation and control of the operating mix is what determines abrasive consumption and surface finish consistency in wheel blast machines.
evidence.source_title: Abrasive blast cleaning practice guidance

interventions.name: Furnace slag to construction aggregate
interventions.summary: Route furnace slag to a cement, block or road construction user instead of to landfill, subject to characterisation and consent.
technical_constraints: Slag chemistry and leachate behaviour vary by melt practice and must be characterised, not assumed
Volumetric stability matters for cementitious use - free lime or expansive phases can cause failure in the receiving product
Requires a named offtaker and regulatory consent
Storage and handling on site must prevent leachate to ground
interventions.circularity_mechanism: Moves a residue out of disposal into another industry's input stream.
interventions.impact_basis: Waste line recalculated with the verified treatment factor for the diverted route. No credit is taken for displaced clinker or virgin aggregate at the receiving plant, per GHG Protocol attribution. Stays POTENTIAL until a named offtaker and consent exist.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: characterisation, consent and any storage change. Haulage terms depend on the commercial deal with the offtaker.
prerequisites: Slag characterisation including leachate and volumetric stability

evidence.claim: Metallurgical slags are used as aggregate and as supplementary cementitious material where chemistry, leachate and volumetric stability are demonstrated to be acceptable.
evidence.source_title: EN 12620: Aggregates for concrete

interventions.name: Sub-metering and monitoring, measurement and analysis
interventions.summary: Install sub-meters on the largest electrical and thermal loads so consumption is attributed to processes rather than to the whole site.
technical_constraints: Requires panel access and a shutdown to fit current transformers
Data is only useful with someone reviewing it - metering without a review routine produces nothing
Meter accuracy class must suit the purpose if the data will support an investment case

required_properties.accuracy_class: suitable for billing-grade decisions where required

interventions.circularity_mechanism: Not a reduction measure in itself - it is the prerequisite that turns every other measure from an assumption into a measured, verifiable result.
interventions.impact_basis: No direct carbon reduction is claimed, and EcoForge does not invent one. Its value is that it replaces the assumed sub-load shares used by the lighting, motor and compressed-air interventions with measured ones, which is the difference between an estimate and a business case. It is recommended when those interventions rely on unconfirmed assumptions.
interventions.cost_basis: INDICATIVE: meters, CTs, wiring and a logging system for a small number of major circuits.

evidence.claim: An energy management system requires energy performance indicators and a measurement plan; metering at the level of significant energy uses is what makes performance improvement verifiable.
evidence.source_title: ISO 50001: Energy management systems - Requirements with guidance for use

evidence.claim: Savings from energy conservation measures are quantified against a measurement and verification plan rather than asserted.
evidence.source_title: International Performance Measurement and Verification Protocol (IPMVP)
